questions.question: On the UNWTO definition, a tourist travels:
options: Outside the usual environment, for less than a year, for purposes not remunerated at the destination
Anywhere, for any length of time
For more than a year, for work

questions.question: A visitor who arrives and leaves on the same day is:
options: A day visitor or excursionist — counted, but spending far less than an overnight tourist
Not counted in tourism statistics at all

questions.question: Inbound tourism counts as an EXPORT because:
options: Tourists take goods home in containers
Foreigners spend foreign money inside our borders — foreign exchange earned while the product stays here
The government classifies all travel as trade

questions.question: The MICE market refers to:
options: Medical, international, cultural and educational travel
Business tourism: meetings, incentives, conferences and events

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY demand-side reasons for tourism growth?
options: Rising real incomes, paid leave, longer healthier retirements, growing middle classes
Jet aircraft, low-cost carriers, package holidays
The internet, online booking, destination marketing

questions.question: The jet aircraft and low-cost carriers grew tourism by:
options: Collapsing the price of distance — a flight that once cost a year's salary now costs a week's

questions.question: South Africa's tourism inflection point of 1994 shows that:
options: Tourism follows peace and openness — the end of apartheid and sanctions turned a pariah into a fast-growing destination

questions.question: The 2020 pandemic taught that tourism is:
options: Fast-growing but fragile — a luxury spend that shocks can shut almost to zero in a quarter

subtopics.title: What Tourism Does to an Economy

questions.question: Tourism's indirect GDP contribution exceeds its direct one because:
options: Of the multiplier — hotels buy local inputs and workers re-spend wages, adding income round after round

questions.question: Tourism suits South Africa's unemployment profile because it:
options: Is labour-intensive, absorbs semi-skilled workers, and reaches rural areas where no factory will locate
Pays the highest wages in the economy

questions.question: The state benefits from tourism through:
options: VAT on every bed-night, business taxes and tourism levies funding services far from any reserve

questions.question: The 'enclave resort' criticism describes:
options: Foreign-owned, import-fed operations where much of each tourist rand exits before it can multiply locally

subtopics.title: South Africa's Profile, IKS and Policy

questions.question: South Africa's anchor tourism product is:
options: Nature and wildlife — the Kruger, the Big Five, Table Mountain, the Drakensberg — with heritage, events and climate alongside

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge systems become tourism products through:
options: Traditional medicine, San tracking and rock art interpretation, storytelling, craft, cuisine and dance — culture turned into livelihood

questions.question: The two policy duties attached to IKS tourism are:
options: Authenticity — culture owned and told by its communities — and benefit-sharing, so the community banks the earnings

questions.question: The 1996 White Paper's division of roles is:
options: The private sector governs, communities lead
Government leads, the private sector delivers, communities must benefit

questions.question: Tourism differs from platinum exports because:
options: The buyer travels to the product, the foreign money stays, and the product never leaves — ready to be sold again tomorrow
Platinum earns rands, tourism earns nothing
Tourists must pay in rands before arriving

questions.question: Your aunt from Soshanguve holidaying in Durban is:
options: An inbound tourist earning foreign exchange
A domestic tourist — rands moving inside the nation, supporting jobs but bringing no new money in

questions.question: One foreign holiday touched a hotel, taxi, park, craft stall, restaurant and guide. The point is that:
options: A single visit feeds many industries at once — unlike a container export on its way to the harbour
Curios are South Africa's main export

questions.question: The lodge's cooks and guides, the farmer supplying its kitchen, and the spaza where workers spend wages are, in order:
options: The direct, indirect and induced rings of tourism employment
The induced, direct and indirect rings
All part of the direct ring

questions.question: A rand of tourism buys more employment than a rand of mining because tourism:
options: Is made of hands and hospitality — beds, meals and stories hire people in numbers, not machines

questions.question: 'An export industry with a village attached' describes:
options: A game reserve employing where no factory will ever locate

questions.question: The bus is full but the village stays poor when:
options: The village is too far from the lodge
The lodge is foreign-owned, food imported and packages paid abroad — the rand multiplies somewhere else

questions.question: Visitors fly eleven hours to South Africa for:
options: What exists only here — wild Big Five, Table Mountain, Robben Island, living indigenous cultures — not for beaches and hotels the world has everywhere
The cheapest hotels in the world

questions.question: 'Culture performed WITH people, not ABOUT them' expresses the rule that:
options: Communities must own the telling of their culture — and bank the earnings from it
Culture should not be part of tourism

questions.question: A correct obstacle-fix pair from the lesson is:
options: Slow visas — e-visas for growth markets like China and India

questions.question: 'Keeping the power on IS tourism marketing' because:
options: A load-shedding video travels the world faster than any advert — reliability is part of the brand
